title: TeamViewer security changes
volume: None on a normal day. Each rule takes one event for one admin change, so a company sees a few a month.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Three custom detection rules for TeamViewer, on the CloudAudit records the library's TeamViewer parser writes from the TeamViewer event log. They make a detection when an admin removes two-factor enforcement from accounts, adds a script token or assigns a user role, the changes that follow a TeamViewer account takeover. Each rule matches sensor type TeamViewer only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's TeamViewer parser and the example bridge in bridges/teamviewer-event-logs first, then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive. Event logging needs a Tensor license and a company admin to turn it on.

How it works:
- The parser writes the event name from TeamViewer's event log, such as ScriptTokenAdded, and the author's email as the user.
- Each rule takes one event name from the EventNames list in TeamViewer's Web API reference: RemovedTFAEnforcementFromAccounts, ScriptTokenAdded and UserRoleAssigned.
- The role rule takes every role assignment. The new role is in the event's details, which the parser keeps in request_parameters, so the rule can't tell an admin role from another.

Tuning:
- If an integration adds script tokens as part of its setup, leave its admin out in the query itself, such as and user_name != 'it-automation@example.com'. A suppression rule would hide Sophos's detections for that account as well.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 6 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 16 to 23 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take.
- The events went in through bridges/teamviewer-event-logs, run once on the lab machine against a local mock of the TeamViewer EventLogging API that served the sample events, and posted to HTTP Ingest as gzipped NDJSON, the way the bridge's README says.

Known gaps:
- The bridge polls, so detections arrive up to one poll interval after the event.
- A user who turns off two-factor on their own account (EditTFAUsage) isn't taken.
